themes_detail.label: Street Infrastructure Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints surged to 70 THIS WEEK—a 559% spike versus the 10.6-week average—suggesting acute pavement, pothole, or sidewalk failures across East Harlem, coinciding with a 967% spike in damaged tree reports (4 complaints this week vs. 0.4 avg) that may indicate weather damage or infrastructure collapse.
evidence: Street Condition complaints: 70 this week vs. 10.6 weekly average (559% spike, z-score 10.84)
Damaged Tree complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Community Board has repeatedly requested street light repairs and DOT funding—signal of long-standing neglect now accelerating
reporting_angles: Walk streets in CD111 to document pothole severity, sidewalk buckling, and tree damage; interview residents about safety risks and mobility barriers
Request DOT emergency response data: has the city deployed repair crews? What is average response time for street condition complaints in East Harlem?

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped 336% to 79 complaints LAST WEEK (vs. 18.1 weekly average), the second-largest spike in the dataset, suggesting a new source of sustained daytime or nighttime noise—potentially construction, traffic, or events.
evidence: Noise - Street/Sidewalk complaints: 79 last week vs. 18.1 weekly average (336% spike, z-score 8.33)
Residential noise complaints remain the second-highest category overall (2,297 in 90 days), indicating a baseline quality-of-life issue now worsening
Spike timing coincides with street infrastructure crisis—may indicate construction, emergency repairs, or heavy machinery activity
reporting_angles: Identify source: cross-reference 311 complaint locations with DOT/DEP work orders, construction permits, or NYPD noise enforcement data
Interview residents on specific blocks with high complaint density about noise timing, loudness, and duration

themes_detail.label: Water System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Sewer complaints spiked 620% to 9 LAST WEEK (vs. 1.2 weekly average), and water conservation complaints jumped 700% to 6 LAST WEEK (vs. 0.8 avg), signaling potential main breaks, pressure loss, or contamination events in East Harlem's water infrastructure.
evidence: Sewer complaints: 9 last week vs. 1.2 weekly average (620% spike, z-score 4.96)
Water Conservation complaints: 6 last week vs. 0.8 weekly average (700% spike, z-score 7.94)
Community Board has made 'Other capital budget request for DEP' repeatedly—signal that water infrastructure is a chronic, under-resourced concern
reporting_angles: Request DEP incident data: were there main breaks, boil water advisories, or pressure loss events in East Harlem last week? Map complaint locations against DEP infrastructure maps
Interview residents about water quality, pressure, and service disruptions; check with local clinics for waterborne illness upticks

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street light condition complaints peaked at 15 TWO WEEKS AGO (380% above the 3.1 weekly average), while the Community Board has repeatedly budgeted for street light repairs—indicating chronic infrastructure decay now flagged as urgent in 311 reports.
evidence: Street Light Condition complaints: 15 two weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average (380% spike, z-score 5.39)
Community Board budget requests explicitly include 'Repair or provide new street lights (Agency: Department of Transportation)' annually—signal of persistent neglect
Darkened streets reduce pedestrian and cyclist safety and may enable street crime
reporting_angles: Nighttime photography/video tour of blocks with highest street light complaints to document outages
Interview DOT about repair timeline and funding allocation; cross-reference with NYPD crime data on blocks with poor lighting

themes_detail.label: Tree Damage & Illegal Tree Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Illegal tree damage complaints spiked to 3 LAST WEEK (2,300% above 0.1 weekly baseline), suggesting targeted illegal cutting, storm damage, or construction impacts on the urban canopy—a signal of either environmental crime or lack of tree protection enforcement.
evidence: Illegal Tree Damage complaints: 3 last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2,300% spike, z-score 8.69)
Damaged Tree complaints: 4 this week vs. 0.4 weekly average (967% spike, z-score 7.49)
Combined signals suggest either weather event or systematic tree removal without permits; 449 DOB permits filed in 90 days—some alterations may impact tree canopy
reporting_angles: Review DOB alteration permits (377 filed) and cross-reference with NYC Parks tree removal requests; identify if construction activity is driving tree loss
Interview Parks Department about enforcement of tree protection during construction; document which blocks have seen tree loss
